heroHeadline: Gilani Sworn In as AJK's 17th PM; Pakistani Drones Cross LoC in Rajouri and Poonch, Infiltration Bid Foiled
heroSubtitle: August 29, 2026: Barrister Iftikhar Gilani was elected 30-14 over PPP's Sardar Mukhtar Khan and sworn in as Azad Jammu & Kashmir's 17th prime minister on August 28, capping a chaotic transition after Nawaz Sharif dropped his original nominee, AJK PML-N President Shah Ghulam Qadir, in Gilani's favour on August 27; Qadir and former AJK PM Raja Farooq Haider had publicly objected. On the security front, the LoC saw its busiest 48-hour stretch since mid-July: three suspected Pakistani drones crossed into Rajouri's Nowshera sector late on August 27-28, Indian Army fire forced them to retreat, and troops separately fired on and are still searching for a suspected infiltrator in the same sector. A second Pakistani drone was tracked over Poonch's Mendhar sector on the evening of August 28 before returning across the border, with a search operation continuing into August 29. Separately in Baramulla's Kunzer, security forces recovered two hand grenades from a fleeing suspect during naka checking on August 28. No casualties were reported in any incident. The ceasefire holds at Day 476 with no confirmed cross-border fire exchange since May 10, 2025. Bilateral freeze remains comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT 'in abeyance' — Pakistan on August 29 urged India to resume IWT technical dialogue, which India continues to link to Pakistan credibly ending cross-border terrorism support.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
